The test image shows a green tomato leaf with white powdery/cottony webby growth on the leaf surface. Key features:
- Upper leaf surface affected
- White, powdery/fluffy material coating the leaf
- Leaf veins still visible through the coating
- No distinct necrotic lesions with defined borders

Top candidates: Powdery_Mildew (white powdery surface growth), Gray_Mold (white/gray fluffy), Leaf_Mold (mold on leaf surfaces).

Let me view one reference from each of my top 4 candidates.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Green tomato leaf with white, powdery/cottony webby coating on the upper surface. Veins visible through the material. No discrete necrotic lesions with defined borders.

- **Powdery_Mildew ref (CDDM_1006)**: Green tomato leaves with discrete white powdery patches — same plant, same type of white surface growth. Good match.

- **Gray_Mold ref (Bugwood_21)**: Fruit with gray-white fluffy mold on cracked tissue — different plant part, different context.

- **Leaf_Mold ref (CDDM_1006)**: Yellow patches on upper leaf surface without white powdery material — not a match.

- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot ref (Bugwood_2)**: Wilting whole plant — completely different presentation.

The white powdery/web-like coating on the upper surface of the green tomato leaf is most consistent with **Powdery Mildew**, which causes white powdery mycelial growth on leaf surfaces.
